title.title: The Courtade–Kumar and Hellinger conjectures
title.subtitle: Claim: among Boolean functions of noisy bits, a single coordinate keeps the most information

plain: Squeeze many noisy bits into one bit: the best summary is simply to copy a single bit, as long conjectured

beats.text: Flip each of $n$ fair bits with probability $\varepsilon$; summarise the originals by one Boolean $f$
The curve is what a single coordinate keeps: $1 - h_2(\varepsilon)$ bits
Claimed: no Boolean $f$ rises above it, at any noise level and any $n$

steps: Measure how fast noise drains the information
Split the cube in half along one coordinate
Show joining the two halves still obeys the bound
Climb one dimension at a time, then add up over time

achievement.label: Courtade–Kumar conjecture (2013)
achievement.context: Before: high-noise ranges only (Samorodnitsky, 2016); balanced case to $\rho \le 0.914$ with computer help (Yu)
achievement.note: The companion also proves the Hellinger conjecture; that paper is not in Lean

verify.detail: In Lean: the sharp contraction and Courtade–Kumar with attainment; not the Hellinger paper
verify.ourCheck: We did not build the Lean or referee the proof

voice.text: The Courtade Kumar conjecture, claimed proved.
Squeeze noisy bits into one bit. Which summary keeps the most information?
Split the cube, join the halves, and climb one dimension at a time.
Claimed: copying one bit is best.

sources.quote: For X uniform on {-1,1}^n, Y its image through independent BSC(eps) noise, and any Boolean f, I(f(X);Y) <= 1 - h_2(eps) bits, attained by a coordinate (Courtade-Kumar)
Courtade and Kumar conjectured in 2013 (IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 2014)
Samorodnitsky (2016) proved it in a high-noise range, Yu pushed the balanced case to correlation $0.914$ with computer assistance
the separate Hellinger paper is not formalized (the Courtade-Kumar bound itself is)
